prompt.context: I was flying back from my client the other night, and working away on my laptop. Beside me was seated a mad scientist, who engaged me in conversation, and was excited to find out I was a consultant. It seems that he has created a perpetual motion machine. It requires no energy, and keeps on going. He wants to know how to make money with it.
prompt.question: How should the mad scientist monetize his perpetual motion machine?

framework: Identify the core benefit of the technology: it is a limitless source of energy
Assess where the greatest demand for energy exists across home, industry, and transport
Select the most attractive market segment to drill into — transport/cars is a strong choice given scale of energy consumption
Analyze market size for the chosen application
Evaluate value proposition and what would drive consumer adoption
Determine pricing strategy based on EVC — savings generated must justify switching to new technology; ensure profitability for manufacturer and consumer
Consider go-to-market: how to approach OEMs such as GM and anticipate their reaction
Address the investment pitch angle: 30-second elevator speech

questions.prompt: What is the size of the opportunity if we focus on the automotive/car market in the US?
questions.guidance: Estimate the number of cars in the US, identify the share using traditional vs. alternative fuel, estimate annual new car purchases, and size the revenue opportunity. The interviewee arrived at approximately $40B.

math.setup: Estimate # of US cars x % traditional fuel x % buying new cars per year x assumed technology price
steps: Approximately 280M people in US at roughly 1 car per 1.5 people gives about 180-200M cars
Assume roughly 90% use traditional fuel giving approximately 170M traditional fuel cars
Assume roughly 10% buy a new car per year giving approximately 17M cars per year
Apply assumed technology price per car to arrive at total market opportunity

questions.prompt: What would convince consumers to buy this technology in their cars?
questions.guidance: Strong answers cover: compelling value proposition (no fuel costs, convenience of never refueling), pricing relative to EVC including fuel savings and time saved refueling, awareness and proof of technology credibility, environmental feel-good factor. Pricing should initially be at a premium and may decline as alternative technologies emerge and competition increases.

questions.prompt: What would GM think if you approached them with this technology?
questions.guidance: GM would weigh the threat to their bread-and-butter traditional fuel vehicle business against the first-mover advantage. Key considerations: competitive risk if rivals adopt first, operational and design implementation challenges, need to decide whether to lead or follow. The central tension is cannibalization of existing business vs. competitive necessity.

questions.prompt: Would you invest with the Mad Scientist? Give a 30-second elevator speech to Warren Buffett.
questions.guidance: A strong pitch: This is a source of limitless energy. As global energy demand continues to grow, energy becomes an ever more precious resource. Investing in a limitless source of a precious and increasingly scarce resource offers extraordinary long-term upside. The market spans home, industry, and transport — all massive energy consumers.

brainstorming.prompt: What are the potential applications or markets for a perpetual motion machine (a limitless energy source)?

categories.name: Utilities/Grid
ideas: Selling energy back to the grid

recommendation: Focus initial commercialization on the automotive/transport market given its massive scale and the clear consumer pain point around fuel costs
Approach major OEMs such as GM or Ford with a licensing or partnership model allowing them to integrate the technology into new vehicles
risks: OEMs may be slow to adopt due to threat to existing ICE business model and operational complexity of integration
Technology credibility and proof-of-concept will be a major adoption barrier with consumers and manufacturers
Competitors may develop alternative energy technologies that erode the pricing premium over time
Regulatory and safety certification hurdles for automotive integration
next_steps: Conduct proof-of-concept demonstration for an OEM partner
Define EVC-based pricing model for licensing the technology
Assess IP protection and patent strategy
Pilot in one vehicle segment before broad rollout
